paper.title: LLM-Planner: Few-Shot Grounded Planning for Embodied Agents with Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: A GPT-3 high-level planner for hierarchical embodied instruction following, using 100 paired examples with kNN example retrieval, logit biasing and a grounded re-planning step that injects observed objects after failures or timeouts, achieves competitive ALFRED performance with less than 0.5% of the paired training data while existing trained planners barely work in the same few-shot setting.
paper.scope_note: In scope: LLM high-level planner driving a simulated household mobile-manipulation agent (HLSM low level). Simulation only.

evidence.quote: Despite using less than 0.5% of paired training data, LLM-Planner achieves competitive performance with recent baselines that are trained using the full training data.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim.

evidence.quote: The agent is assumed to be able to enumerate all admissible skills
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap in SayCan: enumerating admissible skills breaks in partially observable environments.

evidence.quote: most existing work [ 1 , 35 , 13 , 24 ] uses LLMs to generate a single static plan from the language instruction and then executes on the entire plan
evidence.support_explanation: Second author gap: static plans are not grounded in the current environment.

evidence.quote: given a high-level plan, low-level planning becomes conditionally independent of the natural language instruction
evidence.support_explanation: Justifies splitting the LLM high-level planner from the low-level planner.

evidence.quote: we adhere to the true few-shot setting [ 28 ] in which prompt design and model selection is conducted via cross-validation on the same small training set instead of using a separate validation set
evidence.support_explanation: Selection protocol: prompt design is chosen by LOOCV on the 100 training pairs, not on the evaluation splits.

evidence.quote: re-planning will be triggered under either of two conditions: 1) the agent fails to execute an action, or 2) after a fixed number of time steps.
evidence.support_explanation: Hand-back rule from low-level executor to the planner.

evidence.quote: we present a simple but effective way to enhance LLMs with physical grounding by injecting a list of observed objects, which may be detected using the object detector of the embodied agent, from the environment into the prompt
evidence.support_explanation: Grounding channel is a list of detected objects only.

evidence.quote: if current subgoal s fails or after n time steps then
evidence.support_explanation: The step threshold n appears in Algorithm 1 but its value is not given in the pinned text (searched Sec 4-5 and Appendix A-D).

evidence.quote: We choose 100 examples for our LLM-Planner among 21,023 ALFRED training examples.
evidence.support_explanation: Few-shot budget.

evidence.quote: we use the public GPT-3 [ 4 ] API with 9 in-context examples chosen from the 100 training examples by the kNN retriever
evidence.support_explanation: Planner configuration: single LLM, 9 retrieved examples.

evidence.quote: We only include objects with a label confidence more than 80 % to reduce noise.
evidence.support_explanation: Detector-derived object list is thresholded; detector is HLSM's perception model.

evidence.quote: we use the pretrained navigation, perception, and depth model from HLSM which are trained using only synthesized trajectories from the simulator, without any paired training data involving natural language instructions or human annotations
evidence.support_explanation: Low-level stack carries no language supervision, so the few-shot claim is limited to the high-level planner.

evidence.quote: We directly replace the trained high-level planner for both models with our LLM-Planner and did not modify any other parts.
evidence.support_explanation: Controlled swap of the high-level planner inside HLSM / FILM.

evidence.quote: it knows all the objects and affordances in the current environment a priori to compile the list of skills
evidence.support_explanation: SayCan baseline is given an oracle advantage, making the comparison conservative for LLM-Planner.
Step-by-step few-shot dynamic row: test-unseen SR 16.42 / GC 23.37, test-seen 18.20 / 26.77, valid-unseen SR 15.36 and HLP ACC 46.59-68.31 range.
Static counterpart of E015: dynamic re-planning adds +0.59 SR (test unseen), +1.10 (valid unseen) in the step-by-step setting.
Full-data goal-only HLSM (test-unseen SR 20.27) versus few-shot goal-only LLM-Planner 13.41; FILM full-data (step-by-step) test-unseen SR is 27.80.
HLSM retrained on the same 100 pairs: test-unseen SR 0.61.
SayCan valid-unseen SR 9.88 and valid-seen 12.30; no test number because test metadata is prohibited.

evidence.quote: We could not evaluate SayCan on the test split because ALFRED prohibits using the test metadata
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline coverage gap on the test split.

evidence.quote: LLM-Planner calls GPT-3 avg. 7 times per task and SayCan calls it 22 times
evidence.support_explanation: Only cost number reported: LLM calls per task.

evidence.quote: Best Model 40.59 – kNN Retriever 17.48 – Logit Biases 38.10 – Both 13.43
evidence.support_explanation: Linearized ablation of LOOCV HLP accuracy (static planner); labels read as best model / without kNN / without logit biases / without both. Not end-to-end SR.

evidence.quote: because we do not have access to an oracle low-level controller
evidence.support_explanation: Dynamic HLP accuracy is only reported as a range because planner and low-level performance cannot be separated.

evidence.locator: Sec 5.6 Effect of Number of Examples
evidence.quote: It is worth noting that the design choices for the main experiments are not informed by this analysis, to respect the true few-shot setting.
evidence.support_explanation: Post-hoc analyses are kept out of selection.

evidence.quote: we could only get 1.8 % success rate due to the object detector from HLSM often failing to detect the
evidence.support_explanation: Heat-and-Place: 36% HLP accuracy but only 1.8% SR because of detector/low-level failures: the planner is not the binding bottleneck.
Valid-unseen SR scaling versus HLSM: LLM-Planner saturates near 17, HLSM reaches 18.28 only with the full data.

evidence.quote: The final HLP quality can be sensitive to minor design choices in the prompt
evidence.support_explanation: Prompt sensitivity acknowledged; choices made by LOOCV (Appendix C).

evidence.quote: We first ablate the kNN retriever module, by replacing it with a retriever that randomly selects in-context examples from the 100 example set.
evidence.support_explanation: Retriever ablation against random selection (HLP accuracy).

evidence.quote: The dataset consists of 7 task types spanning across 207 unique environments, 115 different object types, and 4,703 tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Benchmark scale; split episode counts are not stated in the pinned text.

signatures.object: The high-level planner of a hierarchical ALFRED agent (replacing HLSM's/FILM's trained high-level planner) as a few-shot GPT-3 prompt.
signatures.information: Goal instruction (and optionally step-by-step instructions), list of 8 allowed high-level actions, 9 kNN-retrieved (instruction, high-level plan) examples from a pool of 100 labelled pairs; no semantic map, no admissible-action list.
signatures.operation: Generate the sequence of (action, object) subgoals with temperature 0 and logit bias 0.1 on allowed tokens; low-level planner executes each subgoal.
signatures.output: High-level plan (HLP) executed by the HLSM low-level planner and perception.
signatures.conditions: True few-shot protocol (design chosen by LOOCV on the 100 pairs); frozen BERT-base retriever over instruction embeddings.
signatures.selection_rule: kNN retrieval by instruction embedding; prompt format and K selected by leave-one-out cross-validation on the 100 pairs.
signatures.persistence: not_applicable: fixed 100-pair pool, nothing written back; no retained-improvement claim.
signatures.claimed_effect: Test-unseen SR 13.41 (goal only) / 16.42 (step-by-step) with 100 pairs, versus 0.61 for HLSM retrained on the same pairs.
signatures.failure_boundary: Low-level planner / detector errors (Heat and Place HLP 36% but SR 1.8%); prompt sensitivity.

signatures.object: Grounded re-planning loop: re-prompt the planner with completed subgoals and the objects seen so far when a subgoal fails or n steps elapse.
signatures.information: Detected-object list (confidence > 0.8) from HLSM's perception; completed subgoal list; no other state.
signatures.operation: On failure/timeout call GPT-3 again for a continuation (new plan from scratch if nothing completed), with logit bias toward observed objects.
signatures.conditions: Trigger = failed action or a fixed number n of steps (n not given); objects accumulate within the episode.
signatures.feedback: executor failure / step cap plus detector output
signatures.claimed_effect: Dynamic over static: +1.83 SR (test unseen, goal only), +0.59 (test unseen, step-by-step), +1.10 (valid unseen).
signatures.failure_boundary: Relies on detector recall; single run; gain small relative to the full gap.

gap.author_gap: Trained instruction-following agents need many paired examples; SayCan-style LLM planners need all admissible skills enumerated up front and many LLM calls; most LLM planners emit one static plan that is not grounded in the current environment.
gap.checked_gap: Supported: the SayCan assumption, the cost of ranking, and static-plan limits are stated with sources and the SayCan comparison is run on ALFRED. The importance of the label-efficiency gap is argued from the baselines' collapse at 100 pairs (HLSM 0.00 valid unseen).
lineage: SayCan [1] (rank admissible skills) and Huang et al. [13] (static LLM plan with action matching) -> hierarchical ALFRED planners HLSM [3], FILM [26], (SL)3 [33] (10% data, T5) -> LLM-Planner (generative HLP + kNN prompts + grounded re-planning)
gap.closest_adjacent: SayCan re-implemented on ALFRED with oracle object/affordance knowledge and the same kNN retriever (valid splits only); (SL)3 not comparable because its code was unavailable.
gap.residue: Grounded, label-efficient high-level planning in partially observable, diverse environments without an admissible-action list.
gap.stakes: Annotation cost per task and the ability to add tasks quickly; LLM call count (7 vs 22).
gap.method_response: Generate plans directly, pick examples by retrieval, constrain tokens by logit bias, and re-plan with observed objects when the executor gets stuck.
gap.remaining_gap: Absolute SR stays 13-18% versus 27-28% for full-data FILM/LEBP; the low-level planner and object detector, not the planner, bound end-to-end SR (E025); HLP accuracy only ~40% static.
gap.current_relevance: Not assessed from later work; no later paper in the pinned local set bears on it.
unresolved: Value of n and how a failed subgoal is detected are unstated.
GPT-3 pretraining exposure to ALFRED text is not discussed.

matches.reason: The task is turned into retrieved in-context conditioning and solved with no parameter updates; the retrieval-as-first-class-input branch of C03 is what the paper actually executes.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C25 step1 responsibility boundary: yes (LLM = language-to-subgoals; low level = navigation/interaction). Step2 typed artifact: yes ((action, object) subgoals from an 8-action vocabulary). Step3 close the loop with obtainable signals: yes (execution failure + detector objects). Step4 ablate the loop: yes (static vs dynamic). Step5 cost: yes (calls per task), latency absent.
matches.success_failure_checks: Failure 'only marginally better than unified baseline': not applicable; loop gains are small (+0.6 to +1.8 SR) but toggled.
matches.reason: A distinct operation: typed subgoal hand-off to a separately built low-level executor with an execution-feedback replan loop; the executor is not a sound solver, hence partial.

rs_pattern.reason: Maps to adapt_via_conditioning with a supporting executor-delegation loop.

executes_pattern.reason: Retrieval-conditioned few-shot planning and an execution-feedback replanning loop are both implemented and toggled.

resolves_problem.reason: Closes the sample-efficiency gap relative to retrained baselines (15.36 vs 0.00 valid unseen at 100 pairs) but not the absolute gap to full-data systems, and physical grounding via an object list adds only ~1 SR point.

condition_checks.note: Output restricted to 8 high-level actions plus objects (prompt list and logit bias) over a deterministic/learned low-level executor, but the executor/detector caps results.
Components toggled individually, but kNN/logit-bias only on HLP accuracy, not SR.
Only one LLM backbone is tested, so backbone dependence is not examined.
Hand-back fires on a failed action or a step cap rather than a calibrated completion detector; benefit measured by static-vs-dynamic.
Detector precision/recall not reported; confidence threshold 0.8 only.
Planner gains depend on the HLSM executor and detector; Heat-and-Place HLP 36% vs SR 1.8%.

unassigned: kNN retrieval of in-context exemplars plus logit-bias output control and object-list-grounded re-prompting (no domain card; K202 covers only the hand-back timing).
revision_proposals: Pending, not applied: candidate sub-pattern 'replan by re-prompting with accumulated observed objects after executor failure' (single paper 2212.04088; 2302.01560 is a second, different instance with description/explanation feedback) - needs a second independent reading before candidate_pattern.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Retrieved few-shot conditioning fixes the output language to a small semantic action vocabulary executed by a separate low-level planner.
pattern_mapping.conditions_and_differences: K104 turns on a reliable deterministic/frozen executor; here the vocabulary restriction is soft (prompt + logit bias) and executor/detector are the bottleneck. Retrieval of exemplars is not part of K104.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Executor runs the current subgoal and hands control back to the LLM planner when it fails or stalls; planner then continues from completed subgoals with new observations.
pattern_mapping.conditions_and_differences: K202's monitor is a success detector or progress rule; here it is an action-failure/step-cap trigger and the added information is detected objects. No success detector is audited.

claims.text: With 100 paired examples LLM-Planner + HLSM is competitive with trained planners and far above trained planners restricted to the same data.
claims.setting: ALFRED test seen/unseen and valid seen/unseen; low-level planner, perception and navigation from HLSM
claims.baseline_control: HLSM and FILM retrained on the same 100 pairs; SayCan (valid only, oracle objects); full-data HLSM, FILM, E.T., HiTUT, M-TRACK, LEBP
claims.selection_vs_test: Prompt format/K chosen by LOOCV on the 100 training pairs; results on unseen splits.
claims.result_denominator: Test-unseen SR 13.41 (goal only) and 16.42 (step-by-step) vs retrained HLSM 0.61, full-data HLSM goal-only 20.27, FILM 27.80, LEBP 28.30, E.T. 8.57, HiTUT 13.87 (step-by-step), M-TRACK 16.29; split episode counts not stated; single run.
counterevidence: Still well below FILM/LEBP; 'competitive' is true against weaker or goal-only full-data baselines only
claims.allowed_conclusion: A 100-pair GPT-3 high-level planner makes an otherwise untrained-language HLSM stack function and reaches roughly two-thirds of full-data goal-only HLSM SR on test unseen, above E.T. and HiTUT and level with M-TRACK; not parity with the strongest trained systems.

claims.text: Grounded re-planning with an observed-object list improves the plan.
claims.setting: Static vs dynamic LLM-Planner on ALFRED
claims.result_denominator: SR deltas +1.83 (test unseen goal-only), +0.59 (test unseen step-by-step), +1.10 (valid unseen step-by-step); single runs.
counterevidence: Deltas are small and untested for noise
claims.allowed_conclusion: Dynamic re-planning gives a small, consistent-sign SR gain in all reported splits; magnitude unvalidated.

claims.text: Generative planning needs fewer LLM calls than ranking admissible skills.
claims.setting: ALFRED, SayCan implemented with oracle environment knowledge
claims.result_denominator: 7 vs 22 calls per task; SayCan SR 9.88 (valid unseen) vs 15.36
claims.allowed_conclusion: On ALFRED, with the paper's SayCan re-implementation, the generative planner uses about a third of the calls and achieves higher SR.

claims.text: kNN retrieval and logit biases improve plan accuracy.
claims.setting: LOOCV on the 100 training pairs, static planner, HLP accuracy
claims.result_denominator: 40.59 (best) vs 17.48 / 38.10 / 13.43 for the ablated variants (row labels ambiguous in linearized Table 2)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Retrieval matters strongly for HLP accuracy on the training pool; logit bias helps modestly; end-to-end effect not shown.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop ALFRED simulator success on unseen splits; simulation only, single benchmark, shared HLSM perception, no real-world run.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In ALFRED, a GPT-3 high-level planner built from 100 labelled pairs by kNN prompting, plugged into HLSM, reaches test-unseen SR 13.4-16.4 where the same planner retrained on 100 pairs gets 0.6, and re-planning with observed objects adds about 0.6-1.8 SR; it does not match the best trained ALFRED systems and the grounding component's contribution is small and single-run.
assessment.reproduction: author_report only; no reproduction by us

G.reason: Two concrete, sourced gaps (SayCan's admissible-action enumeration and call cost; static ungrounded plans) plus label-efficiency, with SayCan actually re-implemented on ALFRED, trained planners retrained at 100 pairs and a precise residual (low-level/detector bottleneck, large gap to best full-data systems) stated.

M.reason: Conditional independence of low-level planning from the instruction justifies the split, retrieval and constraint choices are reasoned, and static-vs-dynamic gives distinguishable predictions. Weak point: 'physical grounding' reduces to an object list whose causal role is shown only by +0.6 to +1.8 SR single-run gains and HLP-accuracy ablations.

X.reason: Algorithm 1, prompt parts, retriever, logit bias, models and detector threshold allow rebuilding the system; failure boundaries (executor/detector bottleneck) are shown. Not 4: re-plan step threshold n and the failure criterion are unstated, split sizes absent, dynamic HLP accuracy only a range.

measurement.reason: Simulator-judged ALFRED SR/GC on seen/unseen splits and a defined HLP accuracy; no learned verifier. Not 4: episode counts per split, repeats and per-task trial tables are not given, and the dynamic HLP metric is a range.

causality.reason: High-level planner swapped inside unchanged HLSM; strong baselines retrained on the same 100 pairs; SayCan given oracle objects; static-vs-dynamic toggle. Gaps: kNN/logit-bias only on HLP accuracy, one LLM, shared low-level stack hides interactions, GPT-3 ALFRED exposure unaddressed.

holdout.reason: True few-shot protocol keeps prompt design on LOOCV of the 100 training pairs, post-hoc analyses excluded, and evaluation is on unseen scenes. Not 4: single benchmark/embodiment, no real-world run, LLM pretraining contamination not examined.

statistics.reason: Single run per cell, no variance or CI, deltas of 0.6-1.8 SR untested, split sizes missing; only a task-type breakdown and the HLP-vs-SR bottleneck note exist. Anchor v2: no repeats, partial failure decomposition -> 1.

cost.reason: LLM calls per task disclosed (7 vs 22) and supervision budget matched across retrained baselines; SayCan advantaged. Missing tokens, latency, dollars and the cost of the retriever/hyper-parameter search -> 3.
